The only thing it governs is the cost of publishing the order, which was published in the Federal Register of Thursday, January 15, 2026 (91 FR 2045 to 2047, filed 1-14-26), so the clause was performed on publication and nothing remains for it to command. This is performance by the order's own terms, not an end imposed by a later instrument, and the date is the Federal Register issue date shown on the held pages.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 14373 (91 FR 2045 to 2047, January 15, 2026; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14373.txt) in full. The order finds that attachment or other judicial process against the Foreign Government Deposit Funds (Venezuelan government funds held in designated Treasury accounts) would harm national security and foreign policy, declares a national emergency under IEEPA and the NEA (Section 1), defines the funds (Section 2), voids and prohibits attachment and unlicensed dealing and overrides earlier orders to the extent they affect the funds (Section 3), records further findings (Section 4), directs the Secretaries of the Treasury and State and the Attorney General on custody, disbursement and assertion of immunity (Section 5), authorizes rulemaking, agency implementation and congressional reports (Section 6) and states general provisions (Section 7). The prepared inventory of 28 clauses matches the text and is confirmed. The order has no duration or sunset; its only timing words are the effective-date reference in Section 3(b) and the publication-cost provision in Section 7(d). The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) and return zero hits, so no amendment, revocation or supersession is shown. The held-corpus search for the order number finds only the Federal Register copy of the order and two Office of Foreign Assets Control notices of September 30, 2026 (91 FR, issue 188) publishing general licenses that refer to the Foreign Government Deposit Funds as specified in the order; they are implementing licences issued under Section 3 and are leads, not relied on as a legal basis. Because the national emergency was declared on January 9, 2026, its first anniversary (January 9, 2027) falls after the 2026-10-14 cutoff, so no National Emergencies Act continuation notice was due or could yet exist; the claim relies on the statutory one-year term of a declared emergency unless terminated earlier, whose text is not separately held, and no termination is shown. Twenty-seven clauses are therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route and Section 7(d) is spent by performance on publication. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the National Emergencies Act text is not held and the one-year term is stated as law without a held copy.
